note: Two migration layers. Layer 1 (issue #83, commits 3880cb688 + c5c0f88b2): compact law/regulation prefixes (LegalProvision_<slug> -> LegalProvision_<ABBREV>, <slug>_Par_/_Map_/Cluster_, LegalConcept_ -> Concept_). Layer 2 (issue #192, this PR): Amendment_/AmendmentChain_/AmendmentLink_ IRI shortening -- the long <base_slug> segment is replaced by the law's compact abbreviation (data/law_abbreviations.json) or, for regulations, the Reg_<id> stem recovered from the chain's estleg:amends target; 100462 distinct Amendment-family IRI types renamed across ~11.3k files, 0 collisions, 0 chains skipped. total_renames_applied counts distinct IRI types (the underlying replacement count -- @id definitions plus every estleg:amendedBy reference -- is higher). (A parallel Sanctions_<slug>_Map / Sanction_<slug>_Par_... cleanup is implemented in migrate_uris.py's `sanction` family but NOT applied here -- its definitions live in krr_outputs/sanctions/, outside issue #192's file scope; pass `--legacy` to include it.) last_applied_registry_hash = compute_registry_hash(data/law_abbreviations.json); last_applied_corpus_hash = compute_corpus_hash(get_all_scannable_files()) over the post-Layer-2 corpus as committed here (plus this PR's scripts/migrate_uris.py + scripts/generate_amendment_history.py changes). Unrelated scanned-file edits in later commits will drift last_applied_corpus_hash; `migrate_uris.py apply` detects that and asks for a fresh dry-run. scripts/generate_amendment_history.py now emits the compact Amendment_<ABBREV>_... form natively. Layer 3 (resolve-collisions): registry abbreviations that collide once transliterated by sanitize_id (REÕS/REOS, RÕS/ROS, ÜKS/UKS, TsÜS/TsUS), and #426 deprecated duplicates sharing ids with an unregistered live law (TsMS), were split with a file-scoped rename of the yielding law's own files; see collision_resolutions. last_applied_registry_hash is refreshed whenever this layer rewrites the registry.
